samples.question: The picture shows one flat network drawn on white paper: straight black struts joining round junctions. Three junctions are painted as large coloured hubs - one red, one green and one blue - and every other junction is a small black dot. The whole drawing is one single connected network: starting from any junction you can reach every other junction by walking along struts, and no two struts cross anywhere. Each coloured hub has exactly three struts touching it. Now imagine rubbing out all three coloured hubs at once, each one together with the three struts that touch it, and leaving every other junction and strut exactly where it is. What is left breaks into a number of separate pieces: two junctions belong to the same piece when a chain of remaining struts still joins them, and to different pieces when no chain of remaining struts joins them. The number of pieces left is four, five or six. How many separate pieces are left - four, five or six?
